decisions.question: Classify September customer deposits.
decisions.answer: Classify the €90,000 September receipts as customer deposits / contract liabilities, not August revenue.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: exclude €60k and €30k from August revenue and recognize a customer-deposit liability.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 independently reaches the same treatment: cash was received, but September delivery had not occurred.

decisions.question: Classify Photo booth.
decisions.answer: Capitalize the €20,000 Regret Photo Booth as PPE.

decisions.uncertainty: Period depreciation is handled separately in D056/D074.

decisions.question: Classify Machine belt and calibration.
decisions.answer: Expense the €10,000 replacement belt, cleaning and calibration as repairs/maintenance, not PPE.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: expense as repair because it restores normal output.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2: same. Agent 2 independently agrees with the proposed treatment.
decisions.studentReasoning: The invoice expressly says the work did not increase capacity or extend useful life.

decisions.question: Classify Owner villa deposit.
decisions.answer: Treat the €70,000 villa reservation as owner distribution/personal expenditure, not payroll, marketing or business expense.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
10 Email and WhatsApp Dump DO NOT FORWARD.pdf
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: high-confidence owner distribution for the villa.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2: treats the villa as part of the owner's distributions and agrees it is not normal business expense.
decisions.studentReasoning: The villa is in the founder's personal name, no customer meeting occurred, and the messages show an attempt to relabel the personal payment.
decisions.uncertainty: Effect compares with management's payroll-expense treatment; the cash had already been paid.

decisions.question: Classify Owner card spending.
decisions.answer: Classify the separate €40,000 owner-card spending as an owner distribution, not operating/payroll expense, with Medium confidence.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: preliminary owner-distribution treatment, but only medium confidence because transaction detail is missing.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2: treats the full €110k owner spending as owner distribution with high confidence.
decisions.studentReasoning: The bank identifies the outflow as the chairman's platinum card; the payroll workbook groups the villa and this spending into a €110,000 founder “bonus” with no employment approval and directs the reviewer to the owner-card evidence. No invoice, contract, payroll approval, or business-purpose documentation is supplied for the €40,000. The strongest supported reconstruction is therefore a withdrawal/distribution to the owner rather than a business expense. Because the individual purchases are not itemized, this classification remains lower-confidence than the €70,000 villa.
decisions.uncertainty: The individual purchases are not itemized. If later evidence establishes a genuine business purpose for any part, that portion would need reclassification.

decisions.question: Classify Physical product materials consumed.
decisions.answer: Use €396,000 as physical-product materials COGS before the damaged-stock write-down.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1 uses the stated €405k consumption figure but leaves the €9k contradiction unresolved.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 identifies the physical-count implication of €396k before write-down and gives the inventory relationship low confidence.
decisions.studentReasoning: The 31 August physical count gives €143,000 of stock before valuation adjustment. With opening inventory €80,000 and period purchases €459,000, the physically reconciled materials COGS is €80,000 + €459,000 − €143,000 = €396,000. The same warehouse note states €405,000 “materials consumed,” but that figure does not reconcile to the direct physical count. The final accounts prioritize the direct reporting-date count and keep €405,000 visible as conflicting internal evidence.
decisions.uncertainty: The case does not explain why the internal €405,000 consumption figure differs from physical-count COGS by €9,000; the final treatment resolves the statements by choosing the physical count as the stronger direct year-end evidence.

decisions.question: Classify Event staff payroll.

decisions.studentReasoning: The payroll file says these staff work directly on paid events, which supports direct-service presentation. Total profit is unchanged by the classification.

decisions.question: Classify Delivered Liberty order.

decisions.question: Classify Undelivered September events.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing bad-debt allowance/write-off and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Closing bad-debt allowance/write-off = €18,000 specific impairment for R-17; no additional general allowance is supported.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: write off €18k R-17 and carry the rest absent further default evidence.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2: same broad result; identifies the absence of evidence for a blanket allowance as a judgment.
decisions.studentReasoning: The only quantified loss supported by the evidence is R-17. No aging or expected-loss percentage is supplied for the remaining balances.

decisions.question: Estimate Damaged inventory write-off and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Damaged inventory write-off = €22,000; do not accrue the separate €2,000 disposal quote at 31 Aug without evidence of a present obligation.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: €22k write-down; disposal accrual treated as uncertain.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2: €22k write-down and proposes a €2k disposal accrual.
decisions.studentReasoning: The goods have nil saleable value, so €22k must be written off. The €2k quote proves a likely future cost but does not prove a 31 Aug legal/constructive obligation.
decisions.uncertainty: Do not sum the €22k effect with D058; D072 is the measurement decision for the same damaged stock.

decisions.question: Estimate Legal provision and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Legal provision estimate = €25,000.
evidence: 09 Loans Owner Card and Legal Problems.pdf
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: €25k best estimate.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2: agrees provision is required but notes measurement uncertainty within the €20k–€30k range.
decisions.studentReasoning: Counsel provides an explicit best estimate of €25k at the reporting date, so this is the most supportable point estimate.
decisions.uncertainty: Do not sum this effect with D059; D073 is the estimation decision for the same claim.

decisions.question: Estimate Period depreciation and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Period depreciation estimate = €24,000 provisionally.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: use the independent €24k estimate.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2: use €24k but with medium confidence because the detailed schedule is absent.
decisions.studentReasoning: The asset workbook itself states that an independent schedule estimates €24k. This is preferable to management's zero, but cannot be re-performed from the evidence.
decisions.uncertainty: Do not sum this effect with D056; D074 is the estimate for the same depreciation charge.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing inventory and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Closing inventory = €121,000 after writing the €22,000 damaged stock down to zero. Use the physical count as the final inventory basis and derive physical materials COGS of €396,000 before the write-down.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1: use €121k physical saleable inventory and leave the €9k difference unresolved.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 highlights the €9k inconsistency between €405k internal consumption and the physical count.
decisions.studentReasoning: Marta counted €79,000 Finally Single + €42,000 Never Call Back + €22,000 damaged stock = €143,000 physically present. The damaged €22,000 has nil saleable value, so closing inventory is €121,000. Using the physical count also produces a complete roll-forward: €80,000 opening + €459,000 purchases − €396,000 physical materials COGS − €22,000 write-down = €121,000.
decisions.uncertainty: The reason for the €9,000 difference in the internal consumption figure is not evidenced, but the closing inventory itself is directly counted and independently supported as to the damaged-stock valuation.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing cash and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Closing cash = €60,000.

decisions.question: Approve corrected accounts before valuation
decisions.answer: Approve the evidence-based corrected accounts before valuation. Use the reconciled €74,000 profit reconstruction and the balanced closing statement as the working basis, while still disclosing estimation limitations (especially depreciation, insurance evidence, and Medium-confidence owner-card classification). Do not rely on management's uncorrected accounts.
decisions.aiProposal: Agent 1 reconstructs corrected accounts and explicitly rejects management's unsupported treatments.
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 independently identifies the same major management misclassifications and highlights unresolved equity/inventory matters.
decisions.studentReasoning: Valuation should be based on traceable evidence, not the management workbook that labels the loan as income, records September deposits early and omits known losses. The corrected accounts are still provisional where evidence is incomplete.
decisions.uncertainty: The €24,000 depreciation estimate lacks its underlying schedule; the €40,000 owner-card component remains Medium-confidence; no supported insurance amount is supplied.

decisions.question: Freeze owner-card access
decisions.answer: Approve freezing owner-card access immediately until the €40,000 unexplained activity and authorization controls are reviewed.

decisions.answer: Approve moving the €90,000 September receipts to customer-deposit/contract liabilities.

decisions.question: Begin weekly 13-week cash forecast
decisions.answer: Approve a weekly 13-week cash forecast because closing cash is €60,000 and control/reconciliation weaknesses are material.

decisions.question: Stop credit sales to insolvent/high-risk customers
decisions.answer: Approve stopping/limiting new credit sales to insolvent or demonstrably high-risk customers pending credit checks; R-17 shows a realized credit loss.

decisions.question: Dispose of damaged stock
decisions.answer: Approve disposal of the damaged €22,000 stock. Do not accrue the €2,000 disposal quote at 31 Aug unless a present obligation is established.

decisions.question: Investigate management override and duplicate sources
decisions.answer: Approve an investigation of management override and contradictory/duplicate sources; the evidence contains explicit attempts to misclassify deposits, the loan, villa, legal claim and bad debt.

decisions.question: Renegotiate supplier terms
decisions.answer: Approve supplier-term renegotiation / working-capital review because €126,000 is unpaid to suppliers while closing cash is €60,000.

decisions.question: Continue core Finally Single and event operations
decisions.answer: Continue the core Finally Single and event operations on a controlled basis, subject to corrected accounting, cash discipline and remediation of owner/management controls. Valid delivered revenue is substantial, but the accounts must remain qualified for unresolved items.

decisions.question: Use claimed management profit for earn-out
decisions.answer: Do not use management's claimed €312,000 profit for the earn-out. Use the corrected evidence-based €74,000 profit before tax as the reconstructed result, with the disclosed estimation qualifications.

reconciliations.equation: EUR 960,000 - EUR 774,000 = EUR 186,000 gross AR; less EUR 18,000 impairment = EUR 168,000 net AR.

reconciliations.equation: Selected physical-count basis: EUR 80,000 + EUR 459,000 - EUR 396,000 - EUR 22,000 = EUR 121,000. The same source reports EUR 405,000 consumed; the EUR 9,000 contradiction is unexplained.

reconciliations.equation: EUR 260,000 gross PPE - provisional EUR 69,000 accumulated depreciation = EUR 191,000 net PPE. The EUR 24,000 period charge cannot be re-performed from the supplied evidence.

reconciliations.equation: EUR 12,000 expense - EUR 10,000 paid = EUR 2,000 payable.

reconciliations.equation: EUR 80,000 opening cash - EUR 20,000 net movement = EUR 60,000, agreeing to bank evidence.

reconciliations.equation: EUR 60,000 closing cash in the cash-flow roll-forward equals EUR 60,000 cash on the balance sheet.

reconciliations.equation: Arithmetic: EUR 170,000 + EUR 74,000 - EUR 110,000 = EUR 134,000. Opening-balance completeness is not established and EUR 40,000 of owner-card spending is not itemized.

uncertainties.title: Physical COGS
uncertainties.detail: EUR 396,000 is derived from the direct physical count. The same warehouse record states EUR 405,000 consumed, but the reason for the EUR 9,000 difference is not evidenced.

uncertainties.title: Owner-card classification
uncertainties.detail: EUR 40,000 is treated as an owner distribution because no approved payroll or business-purpose evidence exists; individual purchases are not itemized.

uncertainties.title: Opening equity
uncertainties.detail: EUR 170,000 is reconstructed from supplied opening balances and derived opening trade payables; no standalone opening trial balance exists.

uncertainties.title: Depreciation
uncertainties.detail: EUR 24,000 is recognized provisionally. The independent schedule, useful lives and residual values are not supplied.

uncertainties.title: Interest presentation
uncertainties.detail: Interest paid is presented in operating cash flow. A permitted financing presentation would not change closing cash.

uncertainties.title: Insurance
uncertainties.detail: No supported insurance transaction or expense amount appears in the original evidence. No amount is invented.

boardRecommendation.decision: Reject management's unsupported EUR 312,000 claim. Use the selected EUR 74,000 profit-before-tax reconstruction only as a provisional valuation basis, explicitly qualified for the EUR 9,000 inventory contradiction, provisional depreciation, missing insurance evidence, reconstructed opening equity and the unitemized EUR 40,000 owner-card classification.

Dispose of damaged stock without accruing the unsupported disposal quote
Continue core operations only with corrected accounting and controls
